title: Canopy Architecture, Training and Spatial Uniformity
summary: Cannabis canopy management changes architecture, light interception and microclimate; useful training decisions therefore depend on measured spatial conditions, cultivar response and the production objective.

sections.title: Architecture creates gradients
sections.body: Branch orientation, leaf area and plant spacing change how photons and air move through the canopy. Large cannabis plants can develop position-dependent light exposure and chemistry, making spatial measurement important for understanding variability.

sections.title: Training response is not universal
sections.body: Pruning and defoliation redistribute growth and leaf area, but a 2025 study reported cultivar-dependent defoliation outcomes while spectral treatments also altered architecture. Named techniques should therefore be evaluated by measured plant response rather than copied as fixed recipes.

sections.title: Uniformity links conditions to flower outcomes
sections.body: A visually level canopy can still contain strong internal light or humidity gradients. Strong uniformity analysis connects flower position with mapped light/environment and resulting yield or chemical measurements before selecting pruning, spacing or supplemental-light corrections.
